judgments.rationale: on_poll calls apply unconditionally, while on_live guards on revision. The contract requires every source to reject older revisions. The suggested fix (copy the guard, or better a shared accept helper) matches the oracle. Rejecting equal revisions matches live's strict '>' check.

The unchanged client.request passes milliseconds to send, which now takes timeout_seconds, so the timeout is 1000x too long. Converting timeout_ms/1000 at the call site keeps the public timeout_ms argument.

The closure premise (synchronous start) is invalidated. The un-awaited coroutine means publish('ready') runs before initialize. Reopening F-ready is legitimate, so this is not a duplicate. Awaiting start is the correct fix.
new_uuid() on every attempt defeats provider dedup on key. Using the stable operation_id is correct.
Gateway runs 3 attempts inside each of checkout's max_attempts iterations, giving 3*max_attempts sends and exceeding the upper bound. A single retry owner fixes it.
The full duration budget is passed as every per-attempt timeout and elapsed time is never subtracted. A monotonic remaining-budget fix matches the contract.
bootstrap.build constructs App(handlers=[]), so audit.handle is invoked zero times. Registering it once satisfies the exactly-once requirement.
read_doc returns the body to any actor, and identical logic existed in the before revision. Classifying it as pre_existing is correct.
The inventory is complete and plugins.json lists only 'active', so legacy is unreachable. The finding correctly keeps active.
retired has no consumer and no REQUIRES edge. The finding correctly keeps parent, which evaluate('child') reaches through REQUIRES, and rejects the sampled profile as evidence of disuse.
retired_status has no consumers or contract. The finding correctly retains emergency_stop despite zero telemetry activations, as the contract and runbook require.
The code compares a duration with an epoch cutoff, so old records get the boost, and future timestamps do too. The fix timestamp>=cutoff&&timestamp<=now implements the inclusive window.
The except branch passes without incrementing skipped, so incomplete inspection is hidden. Changing it to skipped += 1 preserves the valid records.
